claims.exact_statement: For a capped protein birth-death process N in {0,...,M} with unit births, predictable causal accepted birth intensity 0<=lambda_t<=B, and independent per-molecule loss rate gamma, every controller based on periodic, noisy, delayed, or perfect observations obeys liminf_t Pr(N_t<h)>=Z_(h-1)(B/gamma)/Z_M(B/gamma). The no-observation policy lambda=B below M attains equality. Thus observation rate and precision do not improve the low-tail reliability frontier under a fixed pointwise peak birth cap.
assumptions: Births add exactly one target protein.
Accepted protein birth intensity is predictable and bounded pointwise by B.
The count is capped at M.
Each extant protein is lost independently at constant rate gamma>0.
Observation-based control is causal; sensor errors, delays, and schedules affect only the predictable choice of lambda_t.
The objective is stationary/liminf low-copy probability Pr(N<h), not average energy or another task utility.
claims.novelty_boundary: No novelty claim. Bounded-rate domination is established prior art in gene-regulatory stochastic models. Partially observed and controlled-observation MDPs are established; this application says their sensor choices cannot beat the peak-cap floor for this specific monotone tail objective.

costs.observation: Any positive sensor cost is optional under the stated objective; zero sensing attains the frontier.
costs.production: Peak pointwise protein-completion capacity B is charged as the model constraint.
costs.nature_mapping: If sensor cost reduces achievable B, use the experimentally verified reduced cap; no sensor-cost-to-B map is supplied.

claims.falsifier: A process satisfying all listed unit-birth, pointwise-cap, fixed-loss and causal-control assumptions with a low-tail probability below the truncated-Poisson stationary tail; otherwise a biological counterexample must identify which premise fails.
claims.next_gate: Measure pointwise completion bounds, protein-loss rates, and observation delays/precision in one specified circuit; test the cap assumptions before claiming a biological frontier.

claims.exact_statement: In the finite M=10, gamma=1 model, the state-feedback policy lambda_n=10-n has Binomial(10,1/2) stationary law, mean accepted synthesis 5, low tail Pr(N<5)=193/512, and requires 10 exact event-triggered readouts per unit time in a sample-and-hold implementation. If each read costs c translation-equivalent units, its total resource is 5+10c. A no-sensor constant truncated-Poisson controller at equal total resource crosses the feedback tail at q*=5.43244302539278, mean 5.28241343881282, and c*=0.02824134388128 per read; at c=0.03 the constant controller's low tail is 0.37378250614, below the feedback tail 0.376953125.
assumptions: The feedback stationary rates are births 10-n and deaths n on n=0,...,10.
The digital controller reads exact N immediately after each protein birth or death; each read costs c in protein-completion-equivalent units.
The constant comparator has no state observation, truncated-Poisson stationary law, and attempted birth rate q<=10.
Total cost is defined as mean accepted protein births plus c times observation rate; this is an illustrative resource normalization, not a measured biochemical conversion.
claims.novelty_boundary: Not a globally optimal controller result and not a biological finding. It shows that a free-observation equal-average-synthesis comparison can reverse when one explicit sensing cost is charged. Under fixed peak cap alone, the zero-sensor lambda=B policy has a much smaller tail.

costs.feedback_production: 5 accepted protein births per unit time.
costs.feedback_observation: 10 exact event-triggered reads per unit time; total 5+10c.
costs.constant_comparator: No observation cost; accepted births equal stationary mean q*Z_9(q)/Z_10(q).

claims.falsifier: The stationary binomial/truncated-Poisson formulas, event intensity 10, or Decimal root calculation fail under the stated rates and cost definition.
claims.next_gate: Replace the normalized read cost with measured sensor energy/resource use and solve the corresponding noisy/periodic average-cost control problem.
